title: Nidularium innocentii
description: With a bit of Spanish Shawl, Heterocentron elegans meant to trail over the wall and give complementary fuchsia color.

title: Trachycarpus fortunei framing the entry
description: This palm is serving dual purposes here, it both frames the entry at the street, while also giving a bit of visual privacy from cars driving by for the upstairs bedroom window overlooking it.  I also enjoy how this palm really shines when it catches the evening light.

title: Farfugium japonicum aurea-maculata
description: You are either charmed by the spots on this plant, or think it is diseased!  There are no in betweens.  I matched this up with Chinese pots that have very similar spotting on them, in complementary shades of greens, yellow greens and pale blues.  The same pots in different sizes and shapes were used consistently throughout the house and front garden, in lieu of in ground plantings in the very narrow spaces.

title: View back to entry gate
description: This is the reverse view back to the street from the front porch.  The gate is flanked on the right by Blackstem bamboo, which is repeated at the attached raised planter off the house corner.

title: 28 Vallejo St Garden Drainage Detail
description: Detail of decorative french drain at front entry court garden.  Indonesian turquoise blue pebbles are pressed into place over sand and french drain to drain this patio which is below adjacent street level.  The blue of the stone matches the blue of the roof eaves, and gives a textural accent to the patio saltillo and black slate patio.

title: View of terrace and live oak tree
Cotinus coggygria 'Golden Spirit'
description: A lovely change from the more typical purplish red foliage cultivars of the Smoke Bush, and the chartreuse foliage is a wonderful addition for bright shade or morning sun situations, where you might want a large shrub/small tree as a foliage accent.  I should have taken another picture of this a year later, when it had really filled in and made an elegant grace point to the blank wall it was intended to soften.  Nice mellow golden fall color to the foliage as well.

title: Room with a view...
description: The shot from the lower floor family room shows how the rear terrace appears to be floating amongst the trees, and even though there are homes all around, one sees nothing but Oak woodland forest.  The main raised planter in the center of the photo was originally intended to be a fountain spilling into the garden below, but I came to realize how impractical that would be situated under a Quercus agrifolia tree which drops debris year round.  Plus, the quiet without falling water seemed a more desireable quality for this back garden than a waterfall.  The solid floor of this terrace is much more practical for cleaning than a wood deck, especially when dealing with constant leaf fall and damp shade in winter.

title: Chamaedorea microspadix palm at entry planter
description: A great understory palm which continues to send up new stems, and the showy orange berries on the female plants are also quite showy.

title: Entry Gate and Portal at 28 Vallejo St.
description: I like the rhythm of the repeating squares of the gate and inset glass block and the clerestory windows at the entry hall tower, and hoped that bringing an architectural detail out to the gate would help the very small front garden seem more interesting.  I like the idea of gated private front gardens, and would do them more often if I could, but not everyone sees this as the way to go for making a first impression...

title: View of Wall at Street, 28 Vallejo St.
description: This shows how the wall steps down with the grade, yet gives complete privacy inside the courtyard, while allowing a partial glimpse of some of the plantings behind the wall.

title: 28 Vallejo St Entry Courtyard Garden
description: Cross view at entry courtyard across front of the house, showing how built-in planters, paving details, changes in elevation were used to scale down the height of the wall at the street, necessary for privacy of lower level bedroom and bathroom windows, which can be glimpsed on the right side.  A cantilevered ledge seat was created for quiet moments of contemplation.  The tall palm in the pot against the house wall is another species of Chamaedorea, C. costaricana.

title: 28 Vallejo St Rear garden
description: Detail of plantings at central raised planter off main terrace, with Echeveria agavoides, Graptopetalum paraguayense, Billbergia sanderiana, Cyclamen and Illicium floridanumm and pale foliaged Helichrysum petiolare 'Limelight' to trail over the back edge.

title: Palms at Entry to 28 Vallejo St.
Brahea 'Clara' at lower garden
description: Intended to provide both some accent form and color, as well as screen the downslope neighbor's untended garden from view from above.  This palm has such grace and elegance, and deserves wider usage in Bay Area gardens.

title: Containers and plantings at entry, 28 Vallejo St.
description: This front porch landing provides perfect conditions for the plantings in these tall cylinder pots.  The glimpse of the yellow blooming Cymbidium gives no clue that this remains in pristine bloom for 6 months due to being sheltered from the rains.  The Iris confusa 'Chengdu' in the tallest pot is a vision of pale blue orchid-like flowers as it comes into bloom, with 100's open at a time.  The bromeliad is a Vriesea fenestralis cultivar.

title: Stems of Cannomois grandis
description: This restio is planted in pots both at this deck off the kitchen and down below in the main garden.  The tall stems with beautiful coloration and feathery foliage are a graceful kinetic sculpture against the white walls, and also give a bit of screening looking back across the rear house wall towards the uphill neighbor.

title: View of built-in concrete bench at entry walk
description: The wall breaks to allow the existing Coast Live Oak to grow freely, as it is located right on the property line.  A Monstera deliciosa is located in a container behind the built-in cast in place concrete bench, and is intended to grow up the trunk of the Oak tree.

title: 28 Vallejo St Rear Garden,
description: View of lower garden looking east, to final patio and seat/retaining walls and flanking decorative stucco wall featuring Clematis 'Avalanche' in full bloom in December/January.  This photo of the garden was taken approximately 6 months after initial planting, before the garden had really filled in much.  The seat/retaining wall on the left is a perfect place to contemplate the garden setting, and has complete privacy from all the neighbors, while also being out of the wind with a bit of mid day sun.

title: Blechnum gibbum and Euphorbia 'Dolce Vita'
description: Shade plants below the Chamaedorea tepejilote palm.

title: 28 Vallejo St Rear Garden
description: View of central planter at main terrace off family room, also showing the existing Coast Live Oak tree that this terrace was wrapped around to incorporate its shade and screening from view by neighbors across the arroyo.

title: Acanthus spinosissimus in bloom
description: The rear fence was detailed as alternating panels of horizontal Ipe wood slats and white stucco panels to match the house, and bring a bit of architecture into the lower most section of the garden.

title: View of container plants adjacent bench
description: The spotted leaf plant in the pot is a Farfugium japonicum 'aureo-maculata', or spotted Leopard Plant from Japan.  The spots are a living repetition of the dappled shade cast by the Oak above.

title: Bilbergia vittata with Balinese stone lantern
28 Vallejo St Entry Courtyard Garden
description: Close up view of the first landing at entry walk, framing  the view down to courtyard with raised planters full of accent bromeliads, ferns and palms.  I like the idea that this garden is completely private, and a lush contrast to the very pared down look at the street.  From inside, all one can see is the neighbor's trees, and the abundantly lush garden inside. I chose plants that would look good immediately and in the height of winter,  the house went on the market in January.  This Windmill palm has had its trunk stripped to reveal its stripes, Black stem bamboo and New Caledonian Dwarf Tree ferns flank the steps.

title: 28 Vallejo St Garden Entry Planter
description: Design by David Feix. Black stem bamboo, dwarf tree ferns, and Nidularium innocentii bromeliad in combination with Abutilon and Corsican hellebore for winter color in a full shade exposure.  In such a narrow space, I felt it was important to keep a good balance between usable people space and the garden.  By raising up the plants into cubes, it gives them more prominence as well as defining separate volumes of space much more quickly, with the bamboo stalks a particularly useful tool to give light screening and fast vertical dimension to the outdoor rooms of this courtyard and entry corridor/walk.

title: View from upstairs bedroom onto courtyard
description: The shrubby Clerodendrum trichotomum 'Harlequin' and Mathiasella bupleuroides at the inside of the wall, with the Stauntonia hexaphylla vine reaching over from the street.

title: Curved stairs up to main terrace
Echeveria elegans and Dyckia 'Cactus Ranch Red'
28 Vallejo St Built-in planter at terrace
description: A mix of plants from around the world; Geralton Waxflower from Australia in pink bloom, Parrot's Beak from the Canary Islands, a 'Purple Gleam" California poppy yet to bloom, and the lovely summer blooming South African Aloe reitzii  holding court at center stage.

title: Dicksonia antarctica
description: This tree fern was used to provide greenery in a completely shaded nook adjacent the driveway and entry courtyard wall.

title: Succulents at path in lower garden
